|pattern_sh3 = |pattern_so3 = |leftarm3 = 000000 |body3 = 000000 |rightarm3 = 000000 |shorts3 = CCFF00 |socks3 = 000000 }} '''Fotbal Club CFR 1907 Cluj''', commonly known as '''CFR Cluj''' ({{IPA|ro|t͡ʃefeˌre ˈkluʒ}} or {{IPA|ro|ˌt͡ʃefere ˈkluʒ|}}) or simply '''CFR''', is a Romanian professional [[association football|football]] club based in the city of [[Cluj-Napoca]], [[Cluj County]], that competes in the [[Liga I]]. Founded as ''Kolozsvári Vasutas Sport Club'' in 1907, when [[Transylvania]] was part of [[Austria-Hungary]], the club's current name is an [[acronym]] for ''[[Căile Ferate Române]]'' ("Romanian Railways"). Before its promotion to Liga I in [[2004–05 Divizia A|2004]], CFR Cluj primarily competed in the [[Romanian football league system|lower divisions]]. Since then, the club has increasingly relied on [[List of foreign Liga I players|foreign players]] to achieve success. In the [[2005–06 Divizia A|2005–06 season]], CFR participated in its first [[UEFA|European competition]], the [[UEFA Intertoto Cup|Intertoto Cup]], finishing as runners-up. With substantial financial backing from former owner Árpád Pászkány, the club won its first national championship in the [[2007–08 Liga I|2007–08 season]], ending a 17-year dominance by [[Bucharest|capital]]-based teams.{{cite news |last=Hafez |first=Shamoon |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19588706 |title=BBC Sport – Champions League: What can Manchester United expect in Cluj? |work=BBC Sport |access-date=3 October 2012 |archive-date=4 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004030327/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19588706 |url-status=live }} Between [[2017–18 Liga I|2017]] and [[2021–22 Liga I|2022]], "the White and Burgundies" won five consecutive championships. The club has secured 17 domestic trophies, all in the 21st century: eight Liga I titles, five [[Cupa României]], and four [[Supercupa României]]. In addition to becoming a prominent force in [[Football in Romania|Romanian football]], CFR qualified three times each for the [[UEFA Champions League]] and [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] group stages, and twice for the [[UEFA Europa Conference League|Conference League]] group stages. CFR shares a fierce rivalry with local club [[FC Universitatea Cluj|Universitatea Cluj]], with their matches known as ''[[Cluj derby|Derbiul Clujului]]''. In recent years, the club has also developed less intense rivalries, notably with [[FCSB]], as they frequently compete for the Liga I title."}}
